HighLevel A2P 10DLC registration, full walkthrough (thumbnail set v2)

Four new ideas, each built on one pattern that separates winners from losers inside the same channel. I looked at 254 thumbnails: the 10 best and 10 worst (views against the channel's own normal) of 9 creators, 42 more uploads from the last 60 days, and 16 from the HighLevel niche. The counts below come from 7 creators, 70 winners against 70 losers. Ranked by how I expect them to do. My test: 1, 2 and 3. Drop v1.

What the top creators do

  1. Fewer words win. Winners carry 2.6 words on average, losers 3.2, the niche 4.6. Three words or fewer: 53 of 70 winners, 37 of 70 losers.

  2. A drawn system (board, chart, map) is in 16 of 70 winners and 6 of 70 losers. It is the number one video of Hormozi, Ali Abdaal and Ravi.

  3. Words that run behind the head, so the picture has depth: 16 of 70 winners, 3 of 70 losers.

  4. A video frame with a caption loses: 1 of 70 winners, 10 of 70 losers (8 of Hormozi's 10 worst).

  5. Face size does not separate winners from losers (large or very large: 24 of 70 against 27 of 70). What the face stands next to does.

  6. A face and words with nothing else: 11 winners, 21 losers. The 11 that win have a head as tall as the frame or two or three very plain words.

  7. A red box or underline on a word is in 19 losers and 9 winners. A highlight does not rescue weak words.

  8. A command to the viewer: 17 winners, 8 losers. A question or a quote: 0 winners, 7 losers.

  9. White or light ground: 20 of 70 winners, 0 of 16 in the niche. The niche is all dark with red, green and yellow.

  10. The niche does what the top does not: open mouth shock (5 of 16 against 1 of 70), a pointing finger (6 of 16 against 0 of 140), a logo (15 of 16), a stamp or mark (9 of 16).

Ours in the row

Our four at search size among 8 of the strongest outliers I analysed and 4 from the HighLevel niche.

Why v1 was weak

  • A2P cannot be read at sidebar size on any of the three. Two of them never say it at all, in a search for A2P.
  • Three thumbnails, one layout: words top left, face right, a card bottom left, the same purple ground. The test cannot tell them apart.
  • A busy purple gradient at the same brightness as the face. The winners stand on black, white or one plain colour.
  • The hero is a UI card with four sizes of small text (or five tiles, or an address bar). At 168 pixels it is grey noise. Dan Martell's two UI screenshot thumbnails are both in his worst 10.
  • The words name features (COPY MY PROMPTS, 5 STEPS, USE A SUBDOMAIN), not what the viewer fears or gets. The face was already big enough, so size was never the problem.
